- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 72.5), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +1.5% above peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (avg > 0.1) but forecast declines, model underestimates; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to match sentiment trend.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., >0.3) after a downtrend, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was negative 3–5 days ago, model often undercorrects; add 0.3–0.7% downward adjustment to forecast.
